subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current source and tests make persisted session defaults intentional, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy changes can be shadowed by old session state.

options.title: Clamp stored session exec policy
options.body: Treat global or agent exec security as the upper bound and clear or clamp stored session fields that exceed it, with upgrade/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep persistence and document reset
options.body: Keep per-session `/exec` persistence as-is and document that operators must clear or patch sessions to enforce changed policy for existing lanes.

options.title: Add explicit operator reset first
options.body: Ship a visible session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Clamp stored session exec policy
recommendation.body: Treat global or agent exec security as the upper bound and clear or clamp stored session fields that exceed it, with upgrade/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history trail for the `/exec` session override behavior and focused tests points to steipete.
